August 15, 2026 – On Friday, the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for August was released.

While views of personal finances saw only minor declines, expected business conditions sank 11% for the short run and 17% for the long run. ## Key Takeaways

1.   The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index preliminary reading fell to 51 in August, a 7.6% decrease from July.

2.   The Current Economic Conditions Index fell 16.0% to 51.8, while the Consumer Expectations Index fell 9.5% to 50.6.
3.   Year-ahead inflation expectations increased from 4.3% from 4.2% in July.

results.content: # Economic Optimism Falls For First Time In 3 Months—As Republican Sentiment Nears 2-Year Low. Ty Roush is a breaking news reporter based in New York City. Views on the U.S. economy fell unexpectedly in August, ending two months of improvement after the war in Iran lowered economic optimism to a record low, according to a widely tracked University of Michigan survey, as sentiment among Republicans fell to its lowest level in nearly two years. The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment reading—a monthly survey of Americans’ views on the economy—fell to 51 in August from 55.2 in July, dropping well below consensus analyst estimates of 54.5, according to FactSet. The University of Michigan's Surveys of ​Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped ​to 51.0 this month from 55.2 in ⁠July, ending two straight months of improvement. ​Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index ​would be at 54.5.

The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

The decline in sentiment occurred across the political spectrum, with an especially big ​month-to-month drop among Republicans.
results.title: US consumer sentiment deteriorates in August

results.content: In a separate report, the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 51.0 this month from 55.2 in July, ending two straight months of improvement. Sentiment deteriorated across the political spectrum, with an especially big month-to-month drop ​among Republicans, a potential sign of trouble for President Donald Trump's party as it seeks to retain control of the U.S. Congress in the November midterm elections.
